doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Missing New York of the 1960s
summary: He misses the New York of the 1960s and finds old clubs closed or changed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, it’s too much pressure for me. I don’t care for it. But I got embroiled in that and I’m glad I came back for that part of it, although it’s died out now, but I’ve always missed New York. And every time I go back there I take a nostalgia walk around and see where the old Birdland was, which is now a girlie joint, and the Metropole is a girlie joint, and some of those places aren’t even there anymore, the Five Spot and — but I think the thing that I really miss about New York is the New York of the 60s and not New York, especially the way it is now.
